toc.title: The AWS services, agents and advantages

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence; RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation; ML: machine learning; MCP: Model Context Protocol; IAM: Identity and Access Management; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud

  • Identify the AWS services and features for GenAI: Bedrock, SageMaker AI, JumpStart, Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents and AgentCore
  • Describe the advantages of AWS GenAI services
  • Describe the benefits of AWS infrastructure: security, compliance, responsibility and safety
  • Describe the cost trade-offs: token pricing, provisioned throughput and custom models

2The AWS services, agents and advantages

Running case

Cedar and Salt Picks Its AWS Tools

  • Cedar and Salt has a small team and wants GenAI fast, without running graphics processing unit (GPU) servers
  • Engineers ask: which AWS service gives us models, which one lets us customize, and which one runs agents?
  • Finance asks what the options cost, and security asks who can see our data
  • Your job: choose the right service for each need

The AWS GenAI Services at a Glance

  • Tools for work and for developers: Amazon Quick, Kiro, AWS Transform
  • Platforms: Amazon Bedrock (models as a service), SageMaker AI (build and customize), AgentCore (run agents)
  • Models: Amazon Nova, other providers' models, JumpStart models
  • Foundation: AWS infrastructure for security, compliance and scale

Exam tip

Models through an API: Bedrock. Build and tune your own: SageMaker AI. Run agents: AgentCore.

Amazon Bedrock: Foundation Models as a Service

  • Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service for secure access to foundation models from leading AI companies
  • You call one API; there are no servers or GPUs to manage
  • Many providers, including Amazon, with tools to compare models on quality and cost
  • Customize a model with your data, by RAG, fine-tuning or distillation
  • Build agents, add guardrails and evaluate results in one place
Exam tip

Many models, one API, no infrastructure: Amazon Bedrock.

What Bedrock Adds Around the Model

Feature What it does Module
Knowledge Bases Connects a model to your documents for RAG 7
Prompt Management Stores and versions prompts 8
Model customization Fine-tuning, continued pre-training, distillation 9
Model Evaluation Compares models and settings 10
Guardrails Filters harmful input and output 11
Agents and AgentCore Builds and runs agents 4, 7
Exam tip

Match the feature to the need: grounding, prompts, tuning, testing, safety or agents.

Amazon Nova [Verify live]

  • Amazon Nova is AWS's own portfolio of AI offerings
  • Nova models: fast, cost-effective foundation models for text and multi-modal needs, including speech
  • Nova Forge: a service to build your own frontier models using Nova
  • Nova Act: a service for agents that automate browser-based workflows
  • As of 5 November 2026: model names and versions change quickly, so check the Nova page
Exam tip

Nova is the family of Amazon-built foundation models.

Amazon SageMaker AI and SageMaker JumpStart

  • SageMaker AI builds, trains and deploys ML and foundation models with managed infrastructure
  • SageMaker JumpStart is a hub of pretrained, open-source models and solution templates
  • From JumpStart you can deploy, fine-tune and evaluate a model
  • You choose instances, training settings and hosting: more control, more to manage
  • Third-party model licenses are your responsibility to review
Exam tip

Pretrained models to deploy or fine-tune yourself: SageMaker JumpStart.

Bedrock or SageMaker AI?

Need Choose
Fastest start, one API, no infrastructure Amazon Bedrock
Several providers' models to compare Amazon Bedrock
Full control of training, instances and hosting SageMaker AI
Deploy and tune an open-source model yourself SageMaker JumpStart
Custom ML models beyond foundation models SageMaker AI
Exam tip

Least effort: Bedrock. Most control: SageMaker AI.

Amazon Quick, Kiro and AWS Transform [Verify live]

Tool What it is Who uses it
Amazon Quick An AI companion for work: research, business insights and automation Business users
Kiro An AI-powered development environment with specs, steering and MCP tools Developers
AWS Transform Agentic AI that speeds up migration and modernization of servers, apps and code IT teams
  • As of 5 November 2026: these products change fast; confirm details on the AWS pages
Exam tip

Ready-made AI for people at work: Quick. For developers: Kiro. For modernizing workloads: AWS Transform.

Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore [Verify live]

Service What it is
Strands Agents A software development kit (SDK) to build and run agents in your own code: tools, MCP support and multi-agent patterns
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore A platform to deploy and operate agents securely at scale, with any framework and any model
  • AgentCore parts: Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Observability and Policy
  • As of 5 November 2026: the AgentCore service list keeps growing
Exam tip

Build an agent in code: Strands Agents. Run and govern agents at scale: AgentCore.

Advantages of Building GenAI on AWS

  • Accessibility and a lower barrier to entry: use models through an API without ML expertise
  • Efficiency and speed to market: ready-made services shorten the path from idea to product
  • Cost-effectiveness: pay per use instead of buying GPUs
  • Business fit: many models and tools, so you can meet your business objectives
  • Scale and security are built in
Exam tip

API access, no GPU purchase, fast to market: the advantages of AWS GenAI services.

3Infrastructure, costs and practice

Benefits of AWS Infrastructure for GenAI [Verify live]

  • Security: data is encrypted; access is controlled with IAM; VPC and PrivateLink keep traffic private
  • Compliance: AWS lists programs such as ISO (International Organization for Standardization), SOC (System and Organization Controls), GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) and HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) eligibility
  • Responsibility and safety: Guardrails, evaluation and monitoring help keep output safe
  • Model providers have no access to Bedrock logs or to your prompts and completions
  • Under shared responsibility, you still manage access and your data
  • As of 5 November 2026: details are on the Amazon Bedrock security pages
Exam tip

AWS secures the platform; you control who can use it and which data goes in.

Cost Trade-Offs of AWS GenAI Services

Choice Benefit Cost trade-off
On-demand tokens Pay per token, only for use; flexible Cost rises with prompt and answer length
Batch inference Discount for jobs that can wait Not for real-time answers
Provisioned Throughput Steady performance and responsiveness, reserved capacity A commitment, paid even when idle
Custom models Fit your domain better Training and storage charges
Region and redundancy Availability and coverage near users, with Amazon CloudFront edge delivery Extra copies and traffic cost more
  • Track spend with AWS Budgets alerts and Cost Explorer analysis
Exam tip

Spiky use: on-demand. Steady, heavy use: provisioned. Jobs that can wait: batch.

What the Exam Asks: AWS Services for GenAI

  • Which service: Bedrock, SageMaker AI, JumpStart, Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents or AgentCore
  • Which advantage: accessibility, lower barrier, speed to market, cost-effectiveness
  • Which benefit: security, compliance, responsibility or safety
  • Which cost choice: on-demand tokens, batch, provisioned throughput or a custom model
  • Which tool for cost: AWS Budgets or Cost Explorer
Exam tip

Name the need first, then the service.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's AWS Stack

Cedar and Salt needs Choose
Models from several providers through one API Amazon Bedrock
Deploy and tune an open-source model with full control SageMaker JumpStart and SageMaker AI
Research and insights for the leadership team Amazon Quick
An AI development environment for engineers Kiro
A framework to code a booking agent Strands Agents
Run and govern agents securely at scale Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Cheaper overnight review summaries Batch inference
An alert when GenAI spend passes a limit AWS Budgets
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

Try It: Compare Two Models in the Bedrock Playground (Optional)

  • Goal: see that models differ in quality, speed and cost, in a practice account
  • Open Amazon Bedrock in the console and, if asked, follow the steps to get access to two models
  • Open the chat playground and send the same review-summary prompt to each model
  • Compare the answers, the response time and the token counts shown
  • Switch to another model and repeat; then note which meets your quality bar at the lowest cost
  • Clean up: nothing is left running; the playground bills only for tokens used
Exam tip

Hands-on work is not tested on this exam, but it makes model trade-offs concrete.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Cedar and Salt wants to try foundation models from several providers through one API, without managing servers. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon SageMaker AI, by training every model from scratch on its own instances
  • BAmazon Bedrock, a fully managed service for access to foundation models
  • CAmazon Rekognition, a service for analyzing images and video
  • DAmazon Polly, a service that turns text into lifelike speech
Show the answer

Answer: B. Bedrock gives secure access to foundation models from many providers through one API with no infrastructure to manage. SageMaker AI means managing training and hosting, and Rekognition and Polly are task-specific services.

S2The data science team wants to deploy a pretrained open-source model and fine-tune it, with full control over instances and hosting. Which AWS option fits best?

  • AAWS Budgets, which sends alerts when cost and usage pass a limit you set
  • BAmazon Lex, which builds conversational chatbots for voice and text channels
  • CAmazon Transcribe, which turns recorded speech into written text with timestamps
  • DAmazon SageMaker JumpStart, a hub of pretrained models for SageMaker AI
Show the answer

Answer: D. JumpStart offers pretrained open-source models that you can deploy, fine-tune and evaluate with SageMaker AI, giving full control over instances and hosting. The other options do not provide or tune models.

S3Which TWO are advantages of building generative AI applications with AWS managed services? (Select TWO.)

  • AA lower barrier to entry, because no ML expertise is needed to call a model
  • BA guarantee that model outputs are always correct
  • CFaster speed to market, because the infrastructure is already built
  • DNo need to ever evaluate or monitor a model
  • ERemoval of every customer security responsibility
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Managed services lower the barrier to entry and shorten the time to market. They do not guarantee correct output, they do not remove the need to evaluate and monitor, and under shared responsibility customers still manage access and data.

S4Which AWS offering is a platform to deploy and operate AI agents securely at scale, with any framework and any model?

  • AAmazon Quick, an AI companion for research and business insights
  • BAWS Glue DataBrew, a visual tool for preparing data
  • CAmazon Bedrock AgentCore, with services such as Runtime and Memory
  • DAmazon Textract, a service that extracts text from documents
Show the answer

Answer: C. AgentCore is an agentic platform for building, deploying and operating agents securely at scale, with services such as Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity and Observability. The other services do different jobs.

S5Cedar and Salt's busy season brings steady, heavy traffic to its assistant, and it needs reliable throughput. Which pricing option fits best?

  • AProvisioned Throughput, which reserves model capacity for a commitment term
  • BOn-demand tokens only, which cannot guarantee any level of capacity
  • CA free tier with no limits, which AWS offers for all foundation models
  • DBatch inference, which returns results later and cannot serve live chats
Show the answer

Answer: A. Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity per model unit for a commitment term, so it suits steady, high-volume workloads that need reliable performance. Batch results arrive later, and on-demand pricing has no capacity commitment.

S6Finance wants an alert when monthly generative AI spending passes a set amount. Which service helps?

  • AAWS Artifact, which provides compliance reports
  • BAWS Budgets, which sets cost thresholds and sends alerts
  • CAmazon CloudFront, which delivers content from edge locations
  • DAWS Config, which records resource configuration changes
Show the answer

Answer: B. AWS Budgets tracks spending against a threshold and sends alerts, and Cost Explorer analyzes where the money went. Artifact, CloudFront and Config do not warn about spending.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Services Bedrock for models as a service, SageMaker AI and JumpStart to build and tune, Quick, Kiro and AWS Transform as tools, Strands Agents and AgentCore for agents
Advantages accessibility, lower barrier, efficiency, speed to market and cost-effectiveness
Infrastructure security, compliance, responsibility and safety, under shared responsibility
Cost on-demand tokens, batch, provisioned throughput, custom models, and Budgets and Cost Explorer to track it
